sentences.en: There's a poem by Philip Larkin called This Be the Verse, and it's been buzzing around in the back of my mind the entire time I've been working on today's interview.
sentences.zh: 菲利普·拉金有一首诗叫《这就是诗》，在我准备今天访谈的整个过程中，它一直在我脑海里盘旋。

sentences.en: The poem starts like this, though literary fans will know I'm swapping in a clean word for a foul one.
sentences.zh: 这首诗是这样开头的，不过文学爱好者会知道，我把一个脏词换成了一个干净的词。

sentences.en: They mess you up, your mom and dad.
sentences.zh: 他们会搞砸你，你的爸爸妈妈。

sentences.en: They may not mean to, but they do.
sentences.zh: 他们可能不是故意的，但他们确实做到了。

sentences.en: They fill you with the faults they had and add some extra just for you.
sentences.zh: 他们把自己的缺点灌输给你，还额外加了一些专门送给你。

sentences.en: That rings true for me, and I bet I'm not alone.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说很真实，我敢说我并不孤单。

sentences.en: But what do we do with that knowledge?
sentences.zh: 但我们该如何处理这些认知呢？

sentences.en: For help answering that question, a lot of people have turned to the work of clinical psychologist Lindsay C.
sentences.zh: 为了寻求这个问题的答案，许多人转向了临床心理学家琳赛·C·吉布森的作品。

sentences.en: Gibson.
sentences.zh: 吉布森。

sentences.en: Her book, Adult Children of Emotionally Immature Parents, has been a slow-burning bestseller, with over a million copies sold since it was published in 2015.
sentences.zh: 她的书《情绪不成熟父母的成年子女》是一本慢热的畅销书，自2015年出版以来销量已超过一百万册。

sentences.en: It's also a viral presence on social media, where it fits in with the larger trend of children
sentences.zh: 它在社交媒体上也引发了病毒式传播，契合了子女们

sentences.en: reconsidering their relationships with their parents, or even if they want to have a relationship with them at all.
sentences.zh: 重新审视与父母关系，甚至考虑是否还要维持这种关系的更大趋势。

sentences.en: So I had lots to ask Dr. Gibson, and some skepticism to bring her to.
sentences.zh: 所以我有很多问题要问吉布森博士，也带着一些怀疑去见她。

sentences.en: We talked about what emotional immaturity looks like in a parent, how much parents really shape
sentences.zh: 我们讨论了父母情绪不成熟的表现，父母在多大程度上塑造了

sentences.en: the adults we become, whether we owe problematic parents compassion, and a bunch of other very easy topics.
sentences.zh: 我们成年后的样子，我们是否应该对有问题的父母抱有同情心，以及其他一系列非常轻松的话题。

sentences.en: Parents, oi.
sentences.zh: 父母啊，哎。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with Lindsay C.
sentences.zh: 这是我和琳赛·C·吉布森的对话。

sentences.en: Gibson.
sentences.zh: 吉布森。

sentences.en: Hi, Lindsay.
sentences.zh: 你好，琳赛。

sentences.en: How are you?
sentences.zh: 你好吗？

sentences.en: Hi, David.
sentences.zh: 你好，大卫。

sentences.en: I'm doing great.
sentences.zh: 我很好。

sentences.en: There are so many things I want to talk to you about.
sentences.zh: 有很多事情我想和你聊聊。

sentences.en: Also, maybe I'll squeeze in a little attempt at getting free therapy from you.
sentences.zh: 另外，也许我会趁机试着从你这里获得一点免费的心理咨询。

sentences.en: That's what I'm here for.
sentences.zh: 我就是为此而来的。

sentences.en: You know, the broad definition of emotionally immature parents are parents who refuse to validate their children's feelings and intuitions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，情绪不成熟父母的广义定义是，那些拒绝认可孩子感受和直觉的父母。

sentences.en: They might be reactive, lacking in empathy or awareness.
sentences.zh: 他们可能反应过度，缺乏同理心或自我意识。

sentences.en: Can you maybe give me a couple sort of specific examples of emotionally immature behaviors from parents?
sentences.zh: 你能给我举几个关于父母情绪不成熟行为的具体例子吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: The biggest one is the egocentrism.
sentences.zh: 最主要的一点是自我中心。

sentences.en: If you just imagine that a person starts and ends all their consideration with what's best for them or how they see things, that's egocentrism.
sentences.zh: 如果你想象一个人所有的考量都始于并终于什么对他最有利，或者他如何看待事物，那就是自我中心。

sentences.en: Um, and, you know, David, I just started watching The Sopranos for the first time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，大卫，我刚开始看《黑道家族》。

sentences.en: I'm like the only person in America that had not watched The Sopranos.
sentences.zh: 我好像是美国唯一一个没看过《黑道家族》的人。

sentences.en: You're in for a treat.
sentences.zh: 你有福了。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I'm on season five now, so I'm, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，嗯，我现在看到第五季了，所以，是的。

sentences.en: Um, but if you listen to the dialogue, they completely nailed it because everything always comes back to the viewpoint of the person who is the emotionally immature character.
sentences.zh: 嗯，但如果你听听里面的对话，他们完全抓住了精髓，因为一切总是回到那个情绪不成熟角色的视角。

sentences.en: It's always all about them.
sentences.zh: 一切总是围绕着他们转。

sentences.en: Another one is, um, the lack of empathy.
sentences.zh: 另一个表现是，嗯，缺乏同理心。

sentences.en: The parent just doesn't get it.
sentences.zh: 父母就是不理解。

sentences.en: They say, why are you so upset about this?
sentences.zh: 他们会说，你为什么为这种事难过？

sentences.en: Or stop it.
sentences.zh: 或者别闹了。

sentences.en: Or this is not a big deal.
sentences.zh: 或者这没什么大不了的。

sentences.en: They cannot enter into the reality of their child's emotional experience.
sentences.zh: 他们无法进入孩子情感体验的现实。

sentences.en: It just doesn't make sense to them.
sentences.zh: 这对他们来说根本说不通。

sentences.en: Maybe it's the teenager who wants to talk to their parent about their girlfriend or boyfriend.
sentences.zh: 也许是一个青少年想和父母谈谈他们的女朋友或男朋友。

sentences.en: And then the parent says, oh, tell me about it.
sentences.zh: 然后父母说，哦，跟我说说。

sentences.en: That reminds me of your father.
sentences.zh: 这让我想起了你父亲。

sentences.en: Let me tell you what he did yesterday.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你他昨天做了什么。

sentences.en: And suddenly, you know, we're back talking about the emotionally immature person's issues with no sense of, you know, sticking to the subject of the other person.
sentences.zh: 突然间，你知道，我们又回到了谈论那个情绪不成熟的人的问题上，完全没有意识到要坚持对方的话题。

sentences.en: Of course, as any parent knows, those characteristics show up even among the best parents sometimes.
sentences.zh: 当然，正如任何父母所知，这些特征有时甚至会出现在最好的父母身上。

sentences.en: How do people distinguish between normal, flawed parental behavior and behavior that's detrimental enough to sort of rise to the label of emotionally immature?
sentences.zh: 人们如何区分正常的、有缺陷的父母行为和足以被贴上情绪不成熟标签的有害行为？

sentences.en: Like, where's the line?
sentences.zh: 比如，界限在哪里？

sentences.en: It's not a clinical diagnosis.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个临床诊断。

sentences.en: So where's the line?
sentences.zh: 所以界限在哪里？

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Where's the line?
sentences.zh: 界限在哪里？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: If you think of emotional maturity and immaturity as being on a continuum, all of us have a spot that we tend to hang out on that continuum.
sentences.zh: 如果你把情绪成熟和不成熟看作是一个连续体，我们每个人在这个连续体上都有一个倾向于停留的位置。

sentences.en: It doesn't mean that we stay there no matter what.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们无论如何都会待在那里。

sentences.en: For instance, like, if you're tired or you're sick or you're stressed, I can guarantee that you are not going to be as emotionally mature as you could
sentences.zh: 例如，如果你累了、病了或者压力很大，我可以保证你不会像在休息好、状态好且没有压力时那样

sentences.en: when you're rested and well and not stressed.
sentences.zh: 情绪成熟。

sentences.en: I mean, that's just what happens.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是会发生的情况。

sentences.en: We all slide down the scale when we have those kinds of stresses.
sentences.zh: 当我们承受这些压力时，我们都会在量表上向下滑动。

sentences.en: However, if you're in one of these other compromised states, you may not be at your finest moment and you may do some things that look immature, but it's going to bother you.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你处于这些受损状态之一，你可能不在最佳状态，也可能做一些看起来不成熟的事情，但这会让你感到困扰。

sentences.en: You're not going to feel okay about what you did.
sentences.zh: 你不会对自己所做的事情感到心安理得。

sentences.en: In fact, you're going to think about what you did.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你会反思自己的行为。

sentences.en: The emotionally immature person, it's like, you know, that was in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 而情绪不成熟的人会觉得，你知道，那已经是过去式了。

sentences.en: That was then.
sentences.zh: 那是当时。

sentences.en: This is now.
sentences.zh: 这是现在。

sentences.en: Why are you wallowing in it and why are you still upset?
sentences.zh: 你为什么还要沉溺其中，为什么还在难过？

sentences.en: The more emotionally mature person would totally get why you're still upset because they have empathy and because they're self-aware emotionally.
sentences.zh: 更情绪成熟的人会完全理解你为什么还在难过，因为他们有同理心，并且在情感上具有自我意识。

sentences.en: They know that you don't get over things just because time passes.
sentences.zh: 他们知道你不会仅仅因为时间的流逝就从事情中走出来。

sentences.en: So they're going to come back and they're going to do something that indicates that they have felt for the other person's experience.
sentences.zh: 所以他们会回来，并做一些事情来表明他们感受到了对方的经历。

sentences.en: You know, my hunch, and you tell me if I'm wrong, is that people are generally arriving at the conclusion that their parents were emotionally immature in their adulthood.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的直觉是——如果我错了请纠正我——人们通常是在成年后才得出父母情绪不成熟的结论。

sentences.en: I think it's sort of like a hindsight situation.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这有点像事后诸葛亮的情况。

sentences.en: If that's true and the adults are feeling, you know, a lack of fulfillment or unhappiness, how do they know that those feelings are the result of their parents' behaviors
sentences.zh: 如果这是真的，而成年人感到缺乏成就感或不快乐，他们怎么知道这些感受是父母行为的结果，

sentences.en: and not the result of any number of other factors that might be causing them to feel the way they do in the current moment?
sentences.zh: 而不是由其他任何可能导致他们当下这种感受的因素造成的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, no, that's a really, that's a great question.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，不，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: I can just tell you what tends to happen in therapy is that the person comes in and they have some immediate issue.
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你心理咨询中通常会发生什么，那就是当事人进来时带着一些直接的问题。

sentences.en: Maybe they're having a problem in their relationship or their work.
sentences.zh: 也许他们在人际关系或工作中遇到了问题。

sentences.en: Maybe they just had a panic attack.
sentences.zh: 也许他们刚刚经历了一次恐慌发作。

sentences.en: They have no idea what's going on.
sentences.zh: 他们完全不知道发生了什么。

sentences.en: And usually, first few sessions, you don't necessarily hear about the parent.
sentences.zh: 通常，前几次咨询你未必会听到关于父母的事情。

sentences.en: But then, you know, like, five, six sessions in, you ask them, you know, before you begin feeling so low, what had happened that evening?
sentences.zh: 但后来，你知道，比如五六次咨询后，你问他们，在开始感到如此低落之前，那天晚上发生了什么？

sentences.en: And then, you know, you come to find out that their dad said something that was completely disrespectful
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，你会发现他们的父亲说了些完全不尊重人的话，

sentences.en: or, you know, whatever, and you begin to, you know, like, make those connections.
sentences.zh: 或者诸如此类的事情，你开始，你知道，建立起这些联系。

sentences.en: What I tended to find out was that when we delved into the feelings, we come to find out that, yeah, they were having very deep reactions to things that their parents did and said.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于发现，当我们深入探讨感受时，我们会发现，是的，他们对父母所做和所说的事情有着非常深刻的反应。

sentences.en: But they had been trained to not see that as legitimate.
sentences.zh: 但他们被训练成不认为那是合理的。

sentences.en: That had been so invalidated, they thought that they were, you know, being disloyal or petty for even bringing it up.
sentences.zh: 那已经被否定得太彻底了，以至于他们认为自己仅仅因为提起这件事就显得不忠或小气。

sentences.en: As a therapist, I would be sitting there and my mind would be going, you know, oh my gosh, that person is so narcissistic that they're describing,
sentences.zh: 作为一名治疗师，我会坐在那里，心里想着，哦天哪，那个人描述的太自恋了，

sentences.en: or she sounds like a borderline personality disorder, but I'm not going to say that to my client.
sentences.zh: 或者她听起来像边缘型人格障碍，但我不会对我的客户那样说。

sentences.en: So I would have to find ways of elaborately translating that into behavior so that we could talk about it without labeling them in a way that made their parents sound pathological.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须想办法把这些复杂地转化为行为，这样我们才能在不给他们贴上让父母听起来有病态标签的情况下讨论它。

sentences.en: Yeah, but isn't labeling someone's parents emotionally immature also a kind of pathologizing?
sentences.zh: 是的，但给某人的父母贴上情绪不成熟的标签不也是一种病态化吗？

sentences.en: I think you could argue that.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以那样争辩。

sentences.en: There's no way of getting around that you're boiling down this person that they love into a set of traits, and it calls them a name.
sentences.zh: 你无法回避这样一个事实：你把他们所爱的人简化为一组特征，并给他们起了一个名字。

sentences.en: It's pejorative.
sentences.zh: 这是贬义的。

sentences.en: But when you say emotionally immature, it's not from the diagnostic manual, and although,
sentences.zh: 但当你说是情绪不成熟时，它不是来自诊断手册，虽然，

sentences.en: yeah, it is a way of categorizing them, but it has a, to me anyway, it has a more explanatory kind of tone to it.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一种分类方式，但对我来说，它有一种更具解释性的语气。

sentences.en: It doesn't, if you say your father is narcissistic, I get an immediate caricature of a narcissiSt.
sentences.zh: 它不会，如果你说你父亲是自恋者，我脑海里立刻会出现一个自恋者的漫画形象。

sentences.en: If I say your father sounds like he may be emotionally immature, I don't know, there's a little bit
sentences.zh: 如果我说你父亲听起来可能情绪不成熟，我不知道，这其中有一点

sentences.en: of grace in that, but I can tell you, David, that a lot of people have a lot of problem when they first hear that idea about their parent.
sentences.zh: 回旋余地，但我可以告诉你，大卫，很多人在第一次听到关于他们父母的这个想法时会有很多困扰。

sentences.en: I've had people come in because of the book that once we get into the therapy part of it,
sentences.zh: 我有一些人因为这本书来咨询，一旦我们进入治疗阶段，

sentences.en: they begin to hedge and balk at calling their parent that because they're just so accustomed to giving their parents the benefit of the doubt.
sentences.zh: 他们就开始回避和抗拒给父母贴上那个标签，因为他们太习惯于给父母留有余地了。

sentences.en: I also am curious about the idea of whether self-identifying as the child of an emotionally immature parent might lead to feelings of victimhood.
sentences.zh: 我也很好奇，将自己定义为情绪不成熟父母的子女是否会导致受害者心态。

sentences.en: Is there any risk in self-identifying as a child of emotionally immature parents and then
sentences.zh: 将自己定义为情绪不成熟父母的子女，然后

sentences.en: feeling disempowered or a lack of agency in your own life and in how you manage your emotions?
sentences.zh: 感到无力或在自己的生活中以及管理情绪方面缺乏自主权，这有风险吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it's exactly the opposite.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为恰恰相反。

sentences.en: I think it really increases a person's sense of agency because what's really disempowering
sentences.zh: 我认为这实际上增强了一个人的自主感，因为真正让他们感到无力的

sentences.en: to them is the idea that I've been trying to interact with my parent using all the communication
sentences.zh: 是这样一种想法：我一直在尝试用我所知道的所有沟通技巧、

sentences.en: skills I know, using all the tact or the empathy that I know, and it doesn't go anywhere and we end up in a fight.
sentences.zh: 用我所知道的所有圆滑或同理心与我的父母互动，但却毫无进展，最终我们还是吵架了。

sentences.en: So they feel the whole basis of a relationship with an emotionally immature person is that you
sentences.zh: 所以他们觉得与情绪不成熟的人建立关系的整个基础就是，你

sentences.en: often feel disempowered because they can't give either you or them the room to have you be understood.
sentences.zh: 经常感到无力，因为他们无法给你或他们自己空间来让你被理解。

sentences.en: And when you realize that the reason that they're not listening, the reason that they don't seem to
sentences.zh: 当你意识到他们不听、他们似乎没有

sentences.en: be responding to you is not because you have poor communication skills, it's because they can't
sentences.zh: 回应你的原因不是因为你沟通技巧差，而是因为他们无法

sentences.en: stand it, they can't bear to be even mildly criticized, they don't have the emotional wherewithal to deal with that.
sentences.zh: 忍受，他们无法承受哪怕轻微的批评，他们没有处理这些问题的情感能力。

sentences.en: And when you realize that, it's like, oh, this is not about my lack of skill or the fact that I get nervous around my parents, that's not the deal.
sentences.zh: 当你意识到这一点时，就会觉得，哦，这不是因为我缺乏技巧或者我在父母面前感到紧张，不是那回事。

sentences.en: And if I understand what's happening, I can change my behavior or I can change my responses because I understand what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 如果我理解了正在发生的事情，我就能改变我的行为或反应，因为我理解他们在做什么。

sentences.en: Back to the Sopranos.
sentences.zh: 回到《黑道家族》。

sentences.en: I mean, those guys were like masters of this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那些家伙简直是这方面的大师。

sentences.en: You complain to them about something and the next thing you know, they're telling you that you're a, you know, a crybaby victim and they didn't do anything to you and you're being

sentences.zh: 休息之后，我回拨了吉布森博士的电话，我们谈论了更多关于同情心，以及人们如何知道他们是否真正快乐。

sentences.zh: 你知道，你曾告诫过不要轻易谈论同情心，因为情感不成熟的人可能会把同情心当作一种诱饵，几乎就像一种“甜蜜陷阱”。

sentences.en: And I say this as someone who is personally fully aware of the pitfalls of extending compassion to the hurtful parent.
sentences.zh: 我这么说，是因为我个人非常清楚对伤害过自己的父母给予同情所带来的隐患。

sentences.en: But at the same time, I want to hold on to the idea that, you know, the emotionally immature person, they're probably struggling, and they're not just boogeymen.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我还是想坚持认为，情感不成熟的人可能也在挣扎，他们并非纯粹的恶魔。

sentences.en: Like, they too deserve grace.
sentences.zh: 他们也值得被宽容。

sentences.en: So how do we open up the door to the possibility of change and reconciliation and understanding
sentences.zh: 那么，我们该如何在没有同情心的情况下，

sentences.en: without compassion?
sentences.zh: 开启改变、和解与理解的大门呢？

sentences.zh: 不，我认为我们不应该在缺乏同情心的情况下做任何事。

sentences.zh: 并不是说我们不想拥有同情心，但我所说的是，在

sentences.zh: 我进行心理治疗的那些人中，也就是这些情感不成熟父母的成年子女，

sentences.zh: 真正的问题在于他们被训练、被施加罪恶感和羞耻感，从而对这些父母产生了过度的同情，明白吗？

sentences.zh: 这没什么邪恶的。

sentences.en: And so when people come to me and they have been conditioned into this sort of compassionate attitude, I take it on myself to have them examine that dynamic.

sentences.en: And so here's a question that I think would elicit different answers from a philosopher or a scientist or a psychologiSt.

sentences.en: Though, in psychotherapy, the biggest change that people seem to have gotten from therapy is that they have a realization of their own inner experience.

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think what I was trying to get at is that if children's basic needs are met, they want to go and do or experience things that make them even happier.
sentences.zh: 我想我试图表达的是，如果孩子们的基本需求得到满足，他们会想要去追求或体验让他们更快乐的事物。

sentences.en: Now, what you're seeing on the playground, though, is a bunch of kids who are navigating a world that could care less about their basic happiness.
sentences.zh: 然而，你在游乐场看到的是一群正在应对一个根本不在乎他们基本幸福的世界的孩子。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Sounds familiar.
sentences.zh: 听起来很耳熟。

sentences.en: Yeah, sounds familiar.
sentences.zh: 是的，听起来很耳熟。

sentences.en: So, as they're, you know, bouncing off of that in their lives, they're going to have all these emotions.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他们在生活中不断碰壁时，他们会产生所有这些情绪。

sentences.en: But the happiness search is, I mean, I think it's why plants reach for the sun.
sentences.zh: 但对幸福的追求，我的意思是，我认为这就像植物向往阳光一样。

sentences.en: I mean, I don't think it's a human thing.
sentences.zh: 我不认为这只是人类的特质。

sentences.en: It's like a universal thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一种普遍的现象。

sentences.en: Like, things that are alive want to flourish.
sentences.zh: 就像活着的东西都想要繁荣生长一样。

sentences.en: They go toward whatever it is that's going to maximize their optimal growth and experience as a living thing.
sentences.zh: 它们会向着任何能最大化其作为生命体的最佳成长和体验的方向前进。

sentences.en: That's what I believe.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的信念。

sentences.en: So, I think that's what little kids are doing.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是小孩子在做的事情。

sentences.en: But, you know, being that they're living in a world in which they have to be, you know, watched and controlled and all of that by parents, they're going to hit all these blocks
sentences.zh: 但是，由于他们生活在一个必须被父母监视、控制的世界里，他们会遇到各种阻碍，

sentences.en: and that's going to make them unhappy.
sentences.zh: 这会让他们感到不快乐。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's certainly not an ideal existence.
sentences.zh: 是的，这当然不是理想的生存状态。

sentences.en: I'm glad I'm out of childhood because a lot of it was a drag, you know.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我告别了童年，因为那段时光里有很多令人沮丧的事情。

sentences.en: But I think that it's important for us to remember that we do have something inside us.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们必须记住，我们内心确实拥有某种东西。

sentences.en: And this is what I would call the core self, which is very based in the body.
sentences.zh: 这就是我所说的“核心自我”，它深深植根于身体之中。

sentences.en: It's very based in emotion.
sentences.zh: 它深深植根于情感之中。

sentences.en: And this core self tells us when we are getting what we need or when we're being treated badly.
sentences.zh: 这个核心自我会告诉我们何时得到了所需，或者何时受到了糟糕的对待。

sentences.en: And how much do you think parents are ultimately responsible for who we become as adults?
sentences.zh: 你认为父母对我们成年后的样子最终负有多大责任？

sentences.en: 53 percent.
Oh, perfect.
sentences.zh: 哦，太完美了。

sentences.en: I'm assuming you really want me to answer that.
sentences.zh: 我假设你是真的想让我回答这个问题。

sentences.en: Of course, yeah.
sentences.zh: 当然，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, I think that, you know, I go back to nature a lot.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想我经常回到自然界去寻找答案。

sentences.en: I go back to plants and animals and trees.
sentences.zh: 我回到植物、动物和树木身上。

sentences.en: And I think that, you know, it's like, how much does it matter to that plant that has its, you know, genetic makeup, you know, that acorn that has the oak tree in it?
sentences.zh: 我想，这就像是，对于那棵拥有特定基因组成的植物，那颗包含着橡树的橡子，它有多重要？

sentences.en: How much does it matter to that acorn or that seed or that animal?
sentences.zh: 对于那颗橡子、那粒种子或那只动物来说，这有多重要？

sentences.en: What does it matter to them how they're treated in the formative years of their life?
sentences.zh: 在它们生命的形成期受到怎样的对待，对它们来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: I would say it matters a lot.
sentences.zh: 我会说这非常重要。

sentences.en: It matters a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 非常重要。

sentences.en: Okay, I was actually kidding when I said 53, because I really think it's much higher than that.
sentences.zh: 好吧，其实我说53%是在开玩笑，因为我真的认为责任比那大得多。

sentences.en: But we have to keep in mind that even if it was 73 percent, that other part, the genetic, the physical,
sentences.zh: 但我们必须记住，即使是73%，剩下的那部分，即基因、生理，

sentences.en: you know, what it is that that child is, you know, bringing into the world as a unique creation, that is huge.
sentences.zh: 那个孩子作为一个独特的个体带到这个世界上的东西，也是巨大的。

sentences.en: And parents cannot take full responsibility for how their kids turn out because of that.
sentences.zh: 因此，父母不能对孩子最终变成什么样负全部责任。

sentences.en: And that I really, you know, that mix I really am not at all sure of.
sentences.zh: 关于这种比例，我确实一点也不确定。

sentences.en: But I do know that you can mess it up early if you don't pay attention to what something needs when it's young.
sentences.zh: 但我确实知道，如果你在某物年幼时不去关注它的需求，你很早就可能把它搞砸。
